references.text: Jeremiah quotes this text almost verbatim in his prophecy against Moab, mentioning that the people of Chemosh will perish, with their sons and daughters taken into captivity.
Jephthah mentions Chemosh as the god of the Moabites in his speech to the king of the Ammonites, referring to how the God of Israel gave them land.
Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable god of the Moabites, showing Chemosh's significance as the national deity of Moab.
Chemosh is mentioned again as the god of the Moabites in connection with Solomon's apostasy and idolatry.
King Josiah destroyed the high places that Solomon had built for Chemosh, the abomination of the Moabites.
The immediate context tells of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who fought against the former king of Moab and took his land.
Jeremiah prophesies that Chemosh himself will go into captivity along with his priests and nobles.
